newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds tighten, junk telecoms active.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds tighten, junk telecoms active.

text.p: Strong buying in U.S. corporate high-grade bonds spurred by a back-up in Treasury yields resulted in tighter spreads across the board, led by bonds of TCI Communications, dealers said.

Investors aiming to lighten positions of Omnipoint Corp debt following a downgrade by Moody's Investors Service sparked moderate trade in high-yields, meanwhile. High-yield bonds on a broader basis were mostly unchanged but spreads tightened as governments fell, traders said.
Back in high-grades, traders said demand was strong across the board with weaker credits getting best bids. Yield bogeys were hit for some large accounts as the Treasury market eroded, they added.

In company specific trade, TCI Communications Inc debt tigthened another five to 10 basis points as dealers began to attached more credibility to rumors that Sprint Corp may move to buy out partners in the Sprint Spectrum venture. The TCI 7-7/8 percent senior noted of 2026 were bid at a 200 basis point spread near the close, in eight basis points on the day.
Dealers said talk of the Sprint move had been lingering for months. Sprint's partners include TCI, Cox Communications Inc and Comcast Corp.

Looking at new issues, Salomon Inc issued $500 million 7.20 percent Baa1/BBB-rated notes due 2004 to yield 81 basis points over the Treasury curve. The debt sold briskly, said sources independent of the deak.
Capital Securities were firm but little changed amid more issuance there, traders said, adding overall trade was light.
"The market has kind of settled in and the inefficiencies have dried up," a trader said. "It's fairly priced."

New trust preferreds included $300 million Baa2/BBB-minus rated 30-year capital securities from Great Western Financial Trust II, priced to yield 135 basis points over the T-bond by lead manager Goldman, Sachs & Co.

Also, Nationsbank Capital Trust III, a unit of Nationsbank Inc, sold $500 million of 30-year, floating rate trust preferred stock at 55 basis points over LIBOR via NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc, Bear Stearns & Co and Lehman Brothers.
Turning to high-yield, Omnipoint Corp's debt fell 1/2 to 3/4 point in moderate trade after Moody's cut its senior note rating to B3 from B2.

Moody's said the risk profile of the company has changed due to its potentially greater future capital needs, its high leverage and the aggressive time frame in which the company must build cash flows needed to meet financial obligations.
At the close, Omnipoint's add-on 11-5/8 percent notes due 2006 were quoted at 104-1/4 bid compared with a 104-3/4 bid, 105-1/4 offer market on Tuesday.
Elsewhere, Sprint Spectrum zeros were active but unchanged for the session after gaining one point on Tuesday. The notes closed at 68-3/4 bid, 69-3/4 offer.

And reflecting the hunt for big yield, Nextlink Communications Inc's $285 million PIK preferred stock traded at 52 to 52-1/2 on Wednesday. The PIK preferreds, done as 5.7 million units, were priced at 50 per unit with a 14 percent dividend rate on Tuesday.

In high-yielding global issues, Argentina issued $2.0 billion 11-3/8 percent 20-year debt to yield 462.5 basis points over the Treasury curve. The deal priced within price talk of 475 to 500 basis points, dealers said.
In the Treasury market, the 30-year bond closed down 19/32 at 95-24/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
